providers_evaluated.java_service: ECS Fargate service behind private target group and public ALB/API boundary
providers_evaluated.python_worker: ECS Fargate private service; one durable poller initially, controlled task launch capability scoped separately
providers_evaluated.static_web: S3 versioned release prefix plus CloudFront; public read-only Web, API calls terminate at Control Plane boundary
providers_evaluated.managed_postgresql: Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL 16-compatible engine; Multi-AZ and instance class require RPF-37 quote/preflight
providers_evaluated.s3_object_storage: Amazon S3 Standard, separate canonical-artifact bucket and least-privilege task role
providers_evaluated.secret_manager: AWS Secrets Manager with ECS secret injection; rotation schedule must be tested before production
providers_evaluated.private_networking: VPC private subnets for RDS, Worker and Control Plane where possible; public edge only at CloudFront/ALB
providers_evaluated.workload_identity: ECS task roles for services; GitHub Actions OIDC for CI/release role with repository/workflow/environment conditions
providers_evaluated.github_deploy_integration: GitHub Actions builds and gates; future release job assumes a narrowly scoped OIDC role only after protected approval
providers_evaluated.approval_release_gate: GitHub Environment production reviewers plus explicit Release Decision and Product Release Identity; no automatic ELIGIBLE deploy
providers_evaluated.health_checks: CloudFront/ALB HTTP check, ECS container checks, Control Plane readiness, Worker heartbeat/backlog, RDS and S3 dependency signals
providers_evaluated.logs_otel: CloudWatch logs/metrics first; optional OTel diagnostics remains non-blocking and bounded
providers_evaluated.rollback: ECS rolling deployment with circuit breaker/alarm rollback to last COMPLETED revision; static Web returns to previous immutable prefix
providers_evaluated.backup_pitr: RDS automated backup and PITR candidate; S3 versioning/lifecycle optional and never replaces application immutability
providers_evaluated.restore_workflow: RDS restore to independent instance, reconnect a disposable stack, verify metadata-artifact consistency; S3 recovery verification separately
providers_evaluated.lowest_practical_monthly_cost: No honest fixed total before region, task-hours, RDS class, ALB/NAT and log volume are known; use a line-item quote
providers_evaluated.free_idle_constraints: Free-tier or promotional credits are not the operating baseline; stopped/idle service and NAT/ALB charges require explicit budget controls
providers_evaluated.operational_complexity: High relative to PaaS, but the cleanest match for scoped IAM, managed persistence, private networking and ECS task isolation
providers_evaluated.vendor_lock_in: Medium: ECS/IAM/ALB/Secrets/CloudWatch are provider-specific; product contracts remain PostgreSQL, S3-compatible, HTTP/JSON and explicit release
providers_evaluated.worker_simulation_fit: Best candidate, but unproven: RPF-28 must be translated to scoped per-run ECS tasks or a separate sandbox host; Docker socket is forbidden

providers_evaluated.python_worker: Render Background Worker, outbound-only and continuously running

providers_evaluated.managed_postgresql: Render Postgres paid tier; recovery and restore behavior is documented, but exact tier/cost requires quote

providers_evaluated.approval_release_gate: GitHub Environment approval can be the authority boundary; provider deploy action must not be triggered by the canonical gate alone

providers_evaluated.logs_otel: Provider logs first; optional OTel export remains diagnostic and may add external cost

region_decision.latency: Not measured from the intended users or GitHub-hosted runner; RPF-37 must run a bounded HTTP/DB/object latency preflight before selection
region_decision.managed_service_availability: AWS documents ap-southeast-1 as Singapore with three Availability Zones and enabled by default; ECS/RDS/S3/Secrets availability and quota still require account-level preflight
region_decision.cost: Regional quote required; no fixed total is claimed
region_decision.data_residency: Singapore candidate. This is not a China-region or legal-residency conclusion; user must approve the geography
region_decision.future_provider_access: Single-region deployment keeps the product contract portable while leaving later provider/region migration possible; no multiregion is proposed
region_decision.maintenance: Use managed services and one region; use Multi-AZ database only after budget approval; keep the Worker and simulation tasks private
decision_gates: user approves Singapore as a data-residency and cost candidate
RPF-28 Controlled Simulation task mapping is proven

selected_topology.name: candidate-b-managed-single-region
selected_topology.diagram: Internet -> CloudFront/static Web -> public API edge -> stateless Control Plane -> private RDS and private S3; private Durable Worker -> Control Plane HTTP/JSON -> scoped per-run Controlled Simulation task -> S3 upload; GitHub Actions -> canonical gate -> protected human approval -> explicit release principal
public_endpoints: Control Plane API edge only when the product needs browser access
health endpoint with no secret or data disclosure
private_endpoints: S3 access through task role/VPC endpoint where cost and account design permit
Worker and per-run simulation task network
data_flows: Web is read-only and fail-closed when canonical API/artifact data is unavailable
Control Plane owns canonical metadata, Job state, Release Decision and artifact verification
Worker owns execution transport but calls Control Plane over HTTP/JSON and never writes DB directly
Simulation task receives only scenario-scoped inputs and cannot access Docker socket, DB credentials or release credentials
Canonical artifact is uploaded before metadata completion and verified by one bounded read
GitHub Actions produces evidence and a future release identity but cannot auto-deploy from ELIGIBLE

access_principals.web_read: read-only browser token or future user session; no worker/decision credential
access_principals.control_plane: service task role plus scoped database and artifact-store access
access_principals.worker: worker service identity with HTTP/JSON and upload permissions only
access_principals.simulation_agent: scenario-scoped tool/environment identity; no database, object-store admin or release access
access_principals.release_principal: separate protected environment identity; only explicit approved release workflow may assume it

web_topology.hosting: static Web on immutable versioned object prefix plus CDN
web_topology.tls_domain: provider-managed TLS at the edge; custom domain is a later authorized configuration
web_topology.api_boundary: browser calls the read-only Control Plane API; no browser-held worker, decision or release credential
web_topology.failure_behavior: API or verified artifact unavailable means fail closed with explicit unavailable state; no fixture fallback outside explicit test mode
web_topology.cache_boundary: cache only public static assets and safe read responses; never cache credentials or mutable authority responses
web_topology.rollback: restore previous Web release prefix and invalidate only affected CDN paths

control_plane_topology.process: stateless Java/Spring service; all canonical state is in managed PostgreSQL and S3-compatible artifact storage
control_plane_topology.restart_replacement: new task must pass liveness/readiness before receiving traffic; no local disk is canonical
control_plane_topology.migration_startup: additive migration check runs before rollout completion; incompatible schema stops readiness and rollout
control_plane_topology.readiness: process, database connection, schema version and artifact-store credential/connectivity checks
control_plane_topology.graceful_shutdown: stop claiming new jobs, heartbeat/finish active attempt within bounded grace, then drain HTTP and exit
control_plane_topology.configuration: externalized environment/provider secret references; no credential in image, source, logs or evidence
control_plane_topology.autoscaling: not claimed in this spike; initial replica is one and scaling is a later measured task

worker_topology.network: outbound-only to Control Plane, simulation-task endpoint and object storage; no public listener
worker_topology.claim_model: existing PostgreSQL-backed durable claim/lease/fencing contract remains canonical
worker_topology.scale_rule: increase replicas only after queue-depth, attempt duration and DB-connection evidence; no broker is introduced
worker_topology.simulation_launch: future provider adapter may launch one scoped ECS task per run or a separately hosted sandbox; it must pass profile identity and cleanup evidence
worker_topology.secrets: worker receives only worker/service credentials and provider task-launch permissions; it never receives release principal or database superuser credentials

controlled_simulation.target_dependency: fresh per-run private network/task with target, dependency, Toxiproxy and Agent-shaped client
controlled_simulation.nested_container: not assumed safe on Render/Railway; AWS candidate requires ECS task-per-run or a separate locked-down sandbox host
controlled_simulation.docker_socket: never mounted into Agent or Worker
controlled_simulation.task_authority: only a narrowly scoped environment-launch identity can create/stop the disposable task; no arbitrary image, subnet or security-group selection
controlled_simulation.cleanup: task and network cleanup must be verified; quarantine on cleanup uncertainty and never silently reuse a foreign resource
controlled_simulation.blocker: provider-specific task isolation and cost/quotas are unproven until RPF-37

managed_postgresql.version: 16-compatible; exact minor and region availability are RPF-37 preflight facts
managed_postgresql.tls: require SSL/TLS and verify the provider CA; force encrypted transport in the application configuration
managed_postgresql.credential_rotation: Secrets Manager rotation candidate; application must support bounded reconnect/pool refresh
managed_postgresql.connection_limit: start with a small per-process pool (5-10) and measure against the selected instance max; do not infer QPS
managed_postgresql.backup: automated backups with a 1-35 day candidate retention; final retention needs product/data policy approval
managed_postgresql.pitr: enabled candidate; restore creates an independent instance and is not considered proven until a rehearsal passes
managed_postgresql.migration: additive expand/contract migrations; no destructive down migration in rollout path
managed_postgresql.exposure: private network only; no public DB endpoint
managed_postgresql.cost: instance, storage, backup, I/O and data transfer are separate line items; exact region quote required

restore_sla_candidate.database_backup_retention: 35 days candidate ceiling, subject to cost and policy approval
restore_sla_candidate.database_rpo: 15 minutes candidate objective, not a provider SLA claim
restore_sla_candidate.database_rto: 4 hours candidate objective for independent restore and application reconnect
restore_sla_candidate.artifact_rpo: provider durability plus application upload-before-metadata; object recovery must be verified separately
restore_sla_candidate.artifact_rto: 4 hours candidate objective for read-back and metadata consistency recovery
restore_sla_candidate.rehearsal_frequency: quarterly and before any destructive migration; first rehearsal is a required RPF-37 gate
restore_sla_candidate.evidence_required: restore target identity, source backup/PITR timestamp, row counts, artifact SHA-256/schema/source checks, reconnect, and cleanup

object_storage.api: AWS SDK S3 API with provider-neutral S3ArtifactStore contract
object_storage.write: conditional If-None-Match create; same-content replay succeeds; different-content same-key conflict fails closed
object_storage.read: one GET followed by RunProof SHA-256, schema, identity and source/runtime verification
object_storage.access: Control Plane/Worker task roles scoped to required prefix and operations; Agent cannot write canonical objects
object_storage.encryption: provider encryption at rest and TLS in transit; KMS choice and cost require RPF-37 authorization
object_storage.versioning: optional defense-in-depth; never substitutes for application immutability or canonical metadata conflict rules
object_storage.lifecycle: candidate transition/retention only after data policy; no automatic delete in this spike
object_storage.restore: object read-back and metadata consistency check; Object Lock is not assumed or enabled by this investigation
object_storage.egress: measure S3-to-compute region locality and public egress; include in cost envelope

s3_compatibility_findings.aws_s3: native candidate not live-tested; existing RPF-32 contract defines required behavior
s3_compatibility_findings.cloudflare_r2: S3-compatible and egress-oriented alternative; existing RPF-32 provider-neutral adapter should be rerun only if this candidate is selected
s3_compatibility_findings.negative_cases: missing, corrupt, wrong identity, invalid access and unavailable endpoint must remain fail-closed
s3_compatibility_findings.status: compatibility contract preserved; no new object-store provider probe executed in RPF-36

artifact_policy.canonical_artifacts: retain long-term by default; deletion requires a later explicit high-risk policy and authority
artifact_policy.orphan_candidate: inventory put-before-metadata objects, keep a seven-day grace period, then require dry-run review before any delete
artifact_policy.delete_authority: separate human/product retention authority, never Agent, Worker or automatic release gate
artifact_policy.gc: not implemented and not authorized in this spike
artifact_policy.metadata_consistency: never delete a canonical artifact solely because a list page is empty; verify metadata and object identity first

secrets.database: platform secret reference injected into Control Plane only
secrets.object_store: task role preferred; static keys only as an explicitly approved transitional boundary
secrets.service_auth: scoped service identity references, rotated independently
secrets.provider_key: platform-managed secret reference injected only into the provider-calling runtime; never persisted in evidence
secrets.release_principal: protected environment/OIDC role reference, never available to Agent or Worker
secrets.rotation: rotate DB/service/provider/release credentials independently and verify reconnect/revocation
secrets.leak_boundary: no Git, image layer, Web bundle, scenario, trace, log, artifact export or TASK_RESULT secret value

service_auth.current: scoped Bearer tokens remain the local/single-tenant compatibility boundary
service_auth.target: mixed transition: provider workload identity for service-to-service and GitHub OIDC for CI/release; preserve explicit scoped HTTP/JSON authority
service_auth.scope: do not implement full OAuth/OIDC/SSO or tenant/RBAC in RPF-36
service_auth.single_tenant: sufficient for first candidate only if user identity is explicitly bounded and no multi-tenant claim is made
service_auth.negative: browser never holds worker/decision/release credential; Agent cannot assume service or release identity

approval_release.recommended: GitHub production Environment with protected reviewers plus a separate release-principal workflow using short-lived OIDC federation
not_allowed: Agent or Worker owns release principal
canonical gate directly mutates provider state
approval_release.trust_policy: restrict repository, main/tag/environment and workflow claims; avoid wildcard subject conditions

product_release_identity.binding: all fields are recorded before deployment and read back from the target; Agent Version Identity remains separate
product_release_identity.immutability: release identity is append-only; rollback points to a prior identity and does not rewrite history
product_release_identity.status: contract designed only; no registry or deployment record created

build_strategy.control_plane: reproducible Java image with pinned base digest and generated SBOM
build_strategy.worker: reproducible Python image with pinned dependencies/base digest and generated SBOM
build_strategy.web: static build with asset manifest and source-tree binding
build_strategy.registry: ECR private repository candidate for selected AWS topology; registry choice remains RPF-37 authorization
build_strategy.digest: deploy by immutable image digest, never mutable latest tag
build_strategy.security_scan: low-cost CI SBOM and vulnerability scan before approval; findings are evidence, not an automatic release authority

schema_migration.ordering: migration-compatible schema first, then application revision; destructive cleanup is a later independent change
schema_migration.failure: migration failure blocks readiness and rollout; it does not auto-run a destructive down migration
schema_migration.rollback: application can roll back while compatibility window remains; schema rollback requires a separate reviewed plan
schema_migration.evidence: migration identity is part of Product Release Identity and target verification

rollout.selected: platform-native ECS rolling deployment with deployment circuit breaker and bounded CloudWatch alarm rollback
rollout.reason: simpler first proof than canary/blue-green while preserving a previous completed revision
rollout.web: publish immutable static prefix, verify, then update edge reference/invalidate bounded paths
rollout.control_plane: new task reaches readiness before old task drains; graceful shutdown stops new job claims
rollout.worker: drain/reclaim active attempts with fencing before replacement
rollout.not_claimed: no canary, multiregion or autoscaling proof in RPF-36

rollback.trigger: failed readiness, deployment circuit breaker/alarm, target verification failure or explicit human decision
rollback.target: previous Product Release Identity with compatible schema/config/secret references
rollback.control_plane: previous image digest and deployment revision
rollback.worker: previous compatible worker image; stale attempts fenced and UNKNOWN_OUTCOME reconciled
rollback.database: restore is not an application rollback; use independent restore rehearsal and explicit data decision
rollback.evidence: record rollback identity, reason, target verification and any data divergence

failure_domains.impact: read-only product unavailable or stale assets
failure_domains.recovery: edge health, asset prefix rollback, cache invalidation
failure_domains.release_impact: block target verification; never mutate canonical evidence
block release and reconcile active jobs

failure_domains.impact: backlog and active attempts may become UNKNOWN_OUTCOME
failure_domains.recovery: lease expiry, stale fencing, bounded reconcile, replacement
failure_domains.release_impact: block completion claim, never blind retry

failure_domains.recovery: provider failover or independent restore rehearsal
bounded retry/reconcile and provider recovery; no metadata completion before verified object

failure_domains.impact: diagnostic signal loss only unless a product audit log is affected
failure_domains.recovery: provider log retention and bounded local export; OTel remains optional
failure_domains.evidence: canonical evidence is independent of diagnostic traces
failure_domains.release_impact: alert; block only if required audit evidence is missing

failure_domains.recovery: rerun with new evidence after cause fixed; no deploy from stale success
failure_domains.release_impact: no release principal assumption without fresh gate

health_readiness.web: edge HTTP 200 for static shell and explicit unavailable state for API failure
health_readiness.control_plane_liveness: process/event loop alive, no secret disclosure
health_readiness.control_plane_readiness: database reachable, expected schema applied, artifact-store verification path available
health_readiness.worker: heartbeat age, claimed attempt age, lease expiry and backlog depth
health_readiness.database: provider health plus bounded application connection/read query
health_readiness.object_store: bounded credentialed verify/read probe without downloading unbounded corpus
health_readiness.graceful_shutdown: stop new claims, heartbeat/reconcile active attempt, drain HTTP, then exit
health_readiness.otel: diagnostic exporter failure does not make the product falsely healthy or block canonical work

observability.logs: provider-managed structured logs with 14-day initial candidate retention and secret/private-protocol redaction
observability.metrics: availability, readiness, job backlog, attempt age, reconcile-required count, DB pool usage, object failure count, release failure count
observability.traces: optional OTel with low-cardinality canonical IDs and bounded retention; no SaaS trace backend required initially
observability.audit: Release Decision, Approval, Product Release Identity and deployment events remain canonical/auditable and are not only OTel data
observability.cost: monitor log ingestion, trace sampling and egress as separate cost lines

minimum_alerts: Control Plane unavailable or readiness failing
PostgreSQL unavailable, connection pool exhaustion or backup failure
Object store unavailable, verification conflict or orphan growth above threshold
Worker heartbeat stale, queue/backlog threshold exceeded or reconcile-required age exceeded
Release target verification or deployment rollback

capacity.evidence_basis: RPF-33 directional measurements only; no Production QPS/SLA claim
capacity.control_plane: one small task initially, 0.5 vCPU / 1 GiB candidate; scale only from observed readiness and DB pool evidence
capacity.worker: one private task, 1 vCPU / 2 GiB candidate, concurrency 1; controlled tasks are separately budgeted
capacity.database: smallest production-eligible RDS class with enough connections for pool and maintenance; exact class is quote/preflight
capacity.connection_pool: 5-10 per process candidate, capped below provider max and measured in RPF-37
capacity.object_storage: 50 GiB soft budget / 100 GiB review threshold candidate; no automatic delete
capacity.cost_envelope: task hours, RDS, ALB/NAT, object storage/requests/egress, logs and backup are measured separately
capacity.broker: BROKER_REQUIRED=NOT_YET; DB-backed durable polling remains the current boundary

backpressure.job_queue: bound claimed concurrency and reject/hold new work when backlog/age threshold is exceeded
backpressure.worker_shortage: leave jobs durable and visible; do not drop or blindly duplicate attempts
backpressure.db_connections: fail readiness or delay claim before exhausting pool; expose pool saturation alert
backpressure.object_upload: bounded retry/reconcile; metadata cannot complete without verified object
backpressure.api_overload: bounded request/page payloads and explicit 429/503 at edge; preserve read fail-closed semantics
backpressure.future_work: capacity/backpressure thresholds need focused RPF-37 measurement, not invented QPS

aws.method: quote required; no fixed monthly total claimed
line_items: CloudFront/S3 static Web storage, requests and transfer
Fargate Control Plane and Worker vCPU/memory seconds
ALB and private-network egress/NAT or VPC endpoints
RDS instance, storage, I/O, backup/PITR and data transfer
S3 artifact storage, PUT/GET/LIST requests, retrieval and egress
Secrets Manager, KMS if selected, CloudWatch logs/metrics and optional traces
aws.formula: monthly = web + fargate + edge/network + rds + object_store + secrets/logs + backup
aws.long_term_baseline: must not rely on promotional credits or free tier

render_r2.lower_bound: about 46 USD/month before paid PostgreSQL, storage, bandwidth and domain: Pro workspace plus three small compute services
render_r2.long_term_baseline: paid Postgres recovery and non-spinning-down compute required; R2 charges are separate

cost_model.portfolio_demo: local Golden Demo remains the no-cloud-cost path; it is not a Production topology or SLA
cost_model.budget_gate: RPF-37 must require a monthly cap, alert threshold, idle-resource shutdown policy and explicit account owner before cloud operations

flow: separate Release principal assumes short-lived identity
ci_release_workflow.current_state: GitHub Actions currently produces CI/evidence only; RPF-36 adds no deploy step
ci_release_workflow.trust_boundary: canonical gate and Agent cannot assume release principal
ci_release_workflow.freshness: release principal requires fresh gate and exact source/image/schema binding; stale result cannot authorize deploy

production_verification_matrix: Web static asset and API fail-closed check
Control Plane readiness, schema and graceful replacement
PostgreSQL TLS, migration, backup/PITR identity and independent restore
S3 conditional put/replay/conflict, verified read and metadata consistency
Durable Job claim, heartbeat, reclaim and response-loss reconcile
RPF-28 Controlled Simulation profile, receipt/effect count and cleanup
Release Decision read-back and separate approval/release authority
Worker and Control Plane restart with no duplicate side effect
rollback to previous Product Release Identity

restore_rehearsal.database: restore a point-in-time backup to a new private instance, apply only forward-compatible migrations, reconnect disposable Control Plane/Worker, compare canonical row counts and decisions
restore_rehearsal.objects: verify retained artifacts by scoped listing/sample and one-GET SHA-256/schema/identity checks; include orphan inventory without deletion
restore_rehearsal.application: run a bounded read/write/reconcile scenario and confirm no release authority is inherited by the rehearsal
restore_rehearsal.exit: record source backup timestamp, restored target identity, result hashes, consistency summary, elapsed time and cleanup
restore_rehearsal.not_done: no provider backup or restore operation executed by RPF-36

data_policy.reviewed_corpus: durable and long-term; historical reviewed bytes immutable
data_policy.jobs_attempts_events: durable canonical operational history; candidate 90-day hot retention requires product approval and later retention plan
data_policy.canonical_artifacts: long-term by default; no automatic GC
data_policy.orphan_artifacts: seven-day candidate grace plus dry-run inventory before separately authorized delete
data_policy.credentials: platform secret references only; values never durable in app data
data_policy.user_identity: first target remains single-user/single-tenant; no multi-tenant identity claim

single_tenant_boundary.public_access: public Web/API edge does not imply multi-tenant readiness
single_tenant_boundary.isolation: one product data domain and one approval boundary; tenant/RBAC remains future scope
single_tenant_boundary.required_before_multi_tenant: tenant identity, authorization model, data partitioning, audit and cross-tenant negative proofs

security_baseline.tls: edge, Control Plane and database/object-store transport encrypted
security_baseline.agent_credentials: no Production credentials and no Docker socket
security_baseline.worker_authority: no Release principal or database direct access
security_baseline.simulation_isolation: private fresh-per-run task/network with verified cleanup
security_baseline.audit_logs: canonical decision/approval/deployment events retained independently of diagnostics
security_baseline.release_separation: human approval and separate release principal required

provider_portability.migration_rule: do not expose provider SDK or credentials through Agent/Product contracts; adapter tests must preserve conditional write, verified read and authority boundaries
